anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De Oratione exists (only copyrighted Greer/O'Meara/Oulton-Chadwick); nothing to compare against. Sense checked against the Greek and cited Scripture wording.

apparatus: Jn 6 discourse the backbone; Ps 107:20; Jn 1:14; Jn 6:58.
1 Cor 3:2; Heb 5:12-14; Rom 14:2 herbs; Prov 15:17; Amos 8:11.
Epiousios coined by evangelists; periousios Ex 19:5; both from ousia.
Stoic-flavored ousia doxography (Diels testimonia in apparatus, not rendered).
Epi+ienai rival etymology judged inferior; today=age texts; Heb 10:1 feasts; Heb 9:26 vs Eph 2:7; Eph 3:20; 1 Cor 2:9; 1 Cor 3:21-22.

choices.why: Kept as 'daily' with transliteration in notes; the chapter judges the ousia-derivation better than epi+ienai — translation follows Origen's verdict.
trōgō = chew/munch; Origen leans on the harshness of Jn 6 — keep it visceral.
The bread's stated end is theosis; literal rendering keeps Origen's claim visible.
Agnosticism about the blasphemer's coming-age economy is load-bearing (apokatastasis horizon without doctrine).

lemmas.lexica: coined; from ἐπί + οὐσία per Origen

pass_a_gloss: The longest chapter: bodily bread impossible (heavenly/great rule); Jn 6 expounded as self-bread and other-bread, flesh for athletes, Word-made-flesh tabernacling; milk/herbs/flesh as soul-lesson grades; simplicity beats heretical loftiness; epiousios coined from ousia (periousios parallel); ousia doxography; bread akin to rational substance imparting immortality; tree of life = Wisdom; angels nourished with Hebrews; Abraham's loaves shared with powers; Christ sups from us then shares; dragon-food makes Ethiopians/serpents; Peter's sheet universalizes nourishment; epi+ienai rival judged worse; today = whole age; feasts shadow ages; ages-puzzle with agnostic blasphemer-economy; superabundant giving; 'our' deferred to last book.

variants.reading: ὁ ζῶν restored in Jn 6:51 quote
